paraphrase: The pre-commit hook re-runs the whole gate, so committing without waiting for tests wastes the developer's time.
Skipping ahead of the test run before a commit is pointless because the hook repeats every check anyway.
Worktrees under .claude/worktrees are gitignored and safe to delete once a task lands.
Once a task merges, the per-task checkout folder can be removed since it was never tracked by git.
Plan verify commands should call pnpm test:unit, never the full suite, because pnpm test spawns a live Codex call.
Use the unit-only test script for a plan's verify step; running the full suite triggers an actual Codex invocation.
A worker nearing its context limit should stop at a clean boundary and report a partial result instead of guessing.
When an agent's context window is almost full, it ought to pause at a good stopping point and flag the work as unfinished.
node:sqlite requires Node 22.16 or newer, so an older runtime must fail with one clear message rather than a stack trace.
Running on a Node version below 22.16 needs to produce a single readable error, not a crash dump, since the built-in SQLite module needs that version.
Force-deleting a git branch is blocked by the bash guard; merge it first and use the plain delete flag.
The shell guard refuses a hard branch removal, so branches must be merged before a normal delete works.
Lessons are append-only: a later insight can supersede an older one but the original text is never rewritten.
The store never edits a lesson's wording after the fact; a newer entry can mark an old one as replaced instead.
Reviewers should flag a pull request that widens scope beyond what the plan's tasks actually own.
When a change touches files outside what a task was granted, that overreach is exactly what review should catch.
The adversary review runs on Codex by default, falling back to an Opus pass when Codex can't be reached.
Codex normally does the adversarial check, but the workflow switches to Opus whenever Codex is unavailable.
Auto memory import should be idempotent, never rewriting files it did not itself create in the memory directory.
Re-running the import of automatic memory must not touch files outside its own directory and must produce the same result each time.
A swarm's lead splits one task into worker briefs and merges their results before verification starts.
In a swarm, the lead agent breaks a task into pieces for workers and combines their output ahead of the verify stage.

The instructions file should stay short, under sixty lines, because the hook layer already covers most of what it would repeat.
